$comment: External monitors for Kiwiply production (REAL-GAPS-C P1.1). The exact definitions to create by hand in UptimeRobot and Healthchecks.io: docs/ops/monitors.md has the click-by-click steps and the alert routes. PLACEHOLDERS ONLY: ping URLs are secrets-by-obscurity and live in the box's .env, never here. A test (scripts/ops/test/workflows.test.sh) checks that every env name below is read by the script named next to it.

email-second.address: OPS_SECOND_EMAIL (placeholder: a second human, so one person on holiday is not a single point of failure)

push.address: UptimeRobot mobile app, Telegram, Pushover or ntfy: any one that makes a phone ring; Healthchecks.io has the same integrations

sev1.meaning: production is down or unreachable (incident-runbook.md section 2)
sev1.response: start now, any hour: docs/ops/incident-runbook.md section 3 and 4H

sev2.meaning: degraded or at risk: a backup, drill, binlog, upload archive or deploy did not report, or the host is short of disk or memory
sev2.response: within the hour: DEPLOY.md section 5.2, the check's own runbook line below

uptimerobot.plan: free is enough: 50 monitors, 5-minute interval, email + mobile push + Telegram/Slack integrations

monitors.name: kiwiply-apex
monitors.detects: the web container, the shared edge Caddy, DNS or TLS for the apex domain
monitors.ifDown: incident-runbook.md section 4H, then DEPLOY.md section 5.4 (deploy.sh --rollback) if the last deploy was the cause

monitors.name: kiwiply-www-redirect
monitors.note: www 301s to the apex (CLAUDE.md); the monitor follows the redirect and passes on the apex's 200, so it proves both the redirect and the target

monitors.name: kiwiply-api-health
monitors.detects: the API container AND its database (the health endpoint is only UP when MySQL answers), plus api.kiwiply.com's route on the shared edge
monitors.ifDown: incident-runbook.md section 4H; the extension calls this host directly, so every signed-in extension user is affected

healthchecks.plan: free is enough: 20 checks, email + Telegram/Pushover/ntfy/Slack integrations. Create each check, copy its ping URL into the box's .env under the variable named here, then reinstall nothing: the scripts read .env on every run.

checks.name: kiwiply-backup
checks.detects: the nightly database dump did not run, failed, or was cut short (a crash, a cut dump, a missing key and a night cron did not run all alert)
checks.ifLate: DEPLOY.md section 5.1; run scripts/ops/backup-db.sh by hand and read /var/log/kiwiply-backup.log. Nothing else matters more: the 2026-09-17 loss started with no backup

checks.name: kiwiply-uploads
checks.detects: the uploads-volume archive (resumes, attachments, PDFs) did not reach the bucket

checks.name: kiwiply-binlog
checks.detects: binary logs stopped reaching S3, which silently turns point-in-time recovery back into 'up to 24 hours lost'

checks.name: kiwiply-host
checks.detects: DISK (85 percent used fails, 90 CRITICAL), memory and swap, container crash loops, TLS certificates under 14 days. It also detects the BOX being down or cron stopped: no ping at all arrives, so this check is the dead-man switch that UptimeRobot cannot be
checks.ifLate: a /fail ping carries the reasons in its body, so the alert email says what is wrong; incident-runbook.md section 2. A check that is late with NO fail ping means the box or cron is down: treat as sev1 if kiwiply-apex is also down
checks.alsoFollow: the body of a /fail is the disk report: 'disk / 91% (CRITICAL)'

checks.name: kiwiply-restore-drill-weekly
checks.detects: the newest backup is older than 2 days, does not match its sha256, or does not restore

checks.name: kiwiply-restore-drill-monthly
checks.detects: the full drill failed: dump plus binlogs do not restore, a hole in the binlog numbering, or an empty user or Liquibase table
checks.ifLate: DEPLOY.md section 5.10; run scripts/ops/restore-drill.sh by hand

checks.name: kiwiply-deploy
checks.cron: none: pinged by each deploy (start, success, fail)
checks.detects: a deploy that failed or was rolled back. Alert on /fail only; the period is long on purpose because deploys are not scheduled
checks.ifLate: n/a: the fail ping says 'deploy <sha> failed: rolled back to ...'; DEPLOY.md section 5.4
